acceptance: Template is a frozen dataclass with the stated fields and raises ParseError for an empty id, not exactly one schedule, every_days below 1, weekdays outside 0-6 or not strictly ascending, no lines, or an end that is not after the start
occurrences of an every_days template are start, start + every_days days, ..., numbered from 1, listed while before end (excluded) and not after until (included)
occurrences of a weekdays template are the days from start on (start included) whose weekday (Monday is 0) is listed, numbered by their count from start, with the same end and until limits

generate places '<template_id>-<number>' orders (template customer, the day, template lines, status open) for the occurrences up to until, leaves out days in skip without renumbering the others, sorts the new orders by day and then template position, adds them to the book in that order and returns them

generate never places an id the book already has (whatever that order is), so a repeated call places nothing and a later call without skip places the skipped occurrences; duplicate template ids raise StockroomError before anything is added

read_templates reads the template CSV (one row per template line, stripped cells, all-empty rows skipped, the rows of one template agreeing on customer, dates, every and weekdays, every as ASCII digits, weekdays as distinct lower-case WEEKDAYS names in any order) and raises ParseError for every problem, including the Template and OrderLine checks
For random templates, untils, skip days and existing orders, occurrences and generate give what the stated rules give

The recur command prints one line per new order and the count line in exactly the stated format; only with --write it rewrites the orders file with write_orders in book order and prints 'wrote ...'; any error ends with exit code 1, 'stockroom: error: ...' on stderr, empty stdout and the orders file unchanged
